newsitem.title: UK: Ogonis reject Shell's offer to fund hospital.
newsitem.headline: Ogonis reject Shell's offer to fund hospital.

text.p: Ogoni activists in Britain reacted angrily on Friday to news that oil company Shell was taking over the maintenance of a hospital in the troubled Ogoni area of Nigeria, calling it a "public relations gimmick".

Royal Dutch Shell Group's activities in the area have been criticised by Ogoni and international pressure groups, particularly since the execution by the Nigerian government last November of nine Ogoni minority rights activists including author Ken Saro-Wiwa.
Shell said in a statement in Lagos on Thursday that it would provide 28 beds and equipment for Gokana hospital's operating theatre and laboratories and provide annual running costs.
The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) said in a statement in London the gesture was timed to coincide with the anniversary of the deaths of the activists.
It came at a period of increased military build-up in Ogoni, MOSOP said.
MOSOP said Shell could demonstrate its support for the Ogoni people by working for the release of imprisoned Ogoni activists.
Shell said on Thursday it had no plans yet to resume oil operations in the area.
